end.summary:
Practised sorting objects that roll, slide, or stack.
Identified curved surfaces as helping objects roll in 6 of 7 unaided attempts.
Identified flat faces for sliding in 2 of 2 attempts.
Identified flat tops and bottoms for stacking in 4 of 5 attempts.
Teach-back was not passed; the idea that only balls roll was corrected through examples of lying bottles, glasses, drums, and boxes.
end.parentNote: Anika practised using the shape and position of an object to predict whether it will roll, slide, or stack. They used examples such as a lying glass, drum, box, and pencil box; the mix-up that only balls roll was corrected later, and they also revised the idea that a round part always prevents stacking. At home, try sorting safe household objects into three groups and ask, “What part touches the surface?”
